```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = TRUE
)
library(verbosity)
```

## Overview

`verbosity` prints structured progress while a script runs:

- `title()` — a centered section header
- `section()` — a timed block whose printed output is indented
- `log_time()` — elapsed time for an expression
- `log_filter()` — row, column, or length changes on a data frame or vector

## Example

```{r example}
title("Subset mtcars example")

section("subset cars", {
  log_time("load data", {
    cars <- mtcars
  })

  log_filter("mpg above 20", cars, {
    cars <- cars[cars$mpg > 20, ]
  })

  head(cars)
})
```

Note: `log_filter()` compares the size of the given variable (before filter) and the result of the expression (after filter).

## Using returned values

`log_time()`, `log_filter()`, and `section()` return the value of the expression. This can be used to store the result in a variable:

```{r returned-values}
option1 <- log_time("load data", {
  mtcars
})

log_time("load data", {
  option2 <- mtcars
})

identical(option1, option2)
```
